title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: October 28 | Week 8 vs. Dallas Cowboys
headline: Jeremiyah Love is limited but practicing and Brissett stays the starter, while Michael Wilson's snaps are being managed through a rotation.
summary: LaFleur said the team wants to get newly added veteran WR 'Zay' up to speed quickly. Jeremiyah Love will be limited but will practice Wednesday. Rookie QB Carson is also limited. He threw well Tuesday and will be tested in 11-on-11 work, and the coach said the QB and medical staff have to weigh playing through pain against risk. Brissett remains the quarterback the team likes best, and the coach said he mostly gets the ball out quickly because that is what the play calls for. LaFleur praised CB Kalen King's mentality and said his arrow is pointing up. He admitted the red zone offense has been a problem and said the team won't shy away from fixing it. He explained that Michael Wilson's snaps in 11 personnel are down because he wants to rotate receivers, saying he doesn't want 70+ plays for 17 straight games. He also called the lower target share for Wilson (and for Marvin Harrison Jr., who is no longer with the team) mostly coincidence. Walt (likely Walter Nolen) was a DNP Wednesday but is improving. The Cowboys, the Week 8 opponent, were described as talented, with a strong defensive line.

injuries.detail: Expected to practice Wednesday in a limited capacity.
Limited this week. He threw well Tuesday, and Wednesday's 11-on-11 work is the next test.
Did not practice (DNP) Wednesday but 'getting better'. The coach said only 'Walt', so the name is inferred.

signals.claim: Will practice in a limited capacity on Wednesday.
signals.note: He is back on the practice field but still limited, so Thursday and Friday participation will decide his Week 8 status.
signals.quote: He'll be limited but he'll be practicing. Yes.

signals.claim: Wilson will keep getting breathers in 11 personnel instead of playing nearly every snap.
signals.note: A deliberate rotation caps his snap share and could limit his volume, though the coach praised him and said the ball is getting to him.
signals.quote: definitely don't want him playing 70 plus plays for 17 straight games.

signals.claim: Brissett remains the starting quarterback over the limited rookie Carson.
signals.note: The coach did not push back on the premise that Brissett gives the team the best chance to win, so his starting job looks secure for now.

signals.claim: Brissett's fast time to throw comes from the intent of the play, not an imposed design.
signals.note: Quick releases support short and intermediate volume for the pass catchers, with deep shots depending on what defenses show.
signals.quote: Jacoby is just trying to do what the intent of the play is

signals.claim: King will keep a significant defensive snap load.
signals.note: Mainly an IDP and defense note, since the coach is high on him and his playing time has been growing.
signals.quote: I think his arrows only pointing up.

signals.note: The coach singled out McBride's win on a route that drew a deep pass-interference penalty against an all-out blitz.
signals.quote: Trey did a great job of winning on his route and drawing the pie.

signals.claim: Did not practice Wednesday but is improving.
signals.note: The status is a concern for defensive-line IDP value this week, though the coach said he is trending up.
signals.quote: He's doing good.

topics.detail: The coach said the offense has not scored in the red zone over the last two weeks. He plans to fix it through practice emphasis, won't go into specifics, and wants the team to push the ball in even from an inch away.

The deeper throws in recent weeks come from defenses playing less shell and forcing the offense to throw over the top. He said explosive plays can also come from yards after the catch and blocking, and cited San Francisco as the model.

Target share for the wide receivers, including the departed Marvin Harrison Jr., is described as a coincidence. Wilson is around eighth in the league in targets, and some weeks you get ten and some weeks four. The coach said Wilson is signed long-term.

A veteran receiver the coach called 'Zay', who was with the team last year, has been brought in as depth. The staff wants to get him up to speed fast, since he already knows the locker room and has played in many offenses.
The coach called Dallas a talent-filled team and singled out its defensive line as a real strength. He also showed respect for Dak Prescott.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Week 8 Media Availability | Wednesday, October 28th | Press Conference
headline: Falcons expect heavy boxes and a tough run defense from Tampa, so efficiency in the run game is the concern; Kyle Pitts was praised as a red zone weapon.
summary: Stefanski opened by saying the injury situation is still in flux and he had few updates. A player he called "OSI" will practice, others are being held out to see how they respond, and some may return Thursday. He explained the recent run-game struggles as the product of facing good defenses and heavier personnel and boxes. His answer was to look for efficiency, block those boxes, and bring receivers down when teams crowd the middle, which opens chances in the pass game. He called Tampa Bay's defense outstanding, saying the tape matches the stats. He expects Todd Bowles to mix heavy boxes with plays from a shell. He brushed off the slow-start numbers, saying the staff needs to give players an early plan they can execute and that the scoreboard matters most. On the quarterback, he said completion percentage matters less than sack avoidance and throwing the ball away, and that the QB's footwork has progressed. He praised Pitts' size, hands and ability to win vertically in the red zone. He called Baker Mayfield a playmaker who can run, and said Tommy Rees continues to do an excellent job as coordinator and play-caller.

signals.claim: Pitts remains a featured red zone target because of his size and ability to win vertically.
signals.note: The coach's praise for Pitts as a red zone jump-ball threat supports his touchdown upside.
signals.quote: Kyle's right in the mix with those guys.

signals.note: Stefanski said Penix's footwork has progressed, which he links to better completions. He framed sack avoidance and throwaways as wins, so completion percentage may stay modest.
signals.quote: we will always put a huge emphasis on quarterback footwork

topics.detail: Stefanski said recent opponents have used heavier personnel and boxes, so the offense is looking for efficiency and needs to block those fronts. When teams close the middle, he sees opportunities in the pass game.
He called the Buccaneers physical, skilled and well coached, and said they are hard to run and throw against. He expects Todd Bowles to use heavy boxes and also play from a shell.

Asked about the league-low first-quarter time of possession, he said every coach wants to start fast. The staff will keep giving players an early plan they can execute, and the scoreboard matters more than time of possession.
Stefanski called Mayfield a playmaker who can run and is extremely talented, and said the game plan requires studying every player on Tampa's roster.
Stefanski praised Rees' play-calling, staff coordination and clear communication on the headset, and described his own role during games as setting the staff up for success.
Stefanski had few updates on a lot of injuries still in flux. A player referred to as OSI will practice, and others are being held out and may return Thursday.

title: Jesse Minter: Us Against the World Mentality
headline: Lamar Jackson got some work in on Wednesday but his status is still open; Minter was optimistic yet noncommittal, and the right guard job is open between Andrew Vorhees and Emery Jones.
summary: Minter called Wednesday's pads practice a good one with a strong response after a loss, and said he took accountability for his own play calls and leadership. On Lamar Jackson, he said Jackson got some work in and that doing more and responding well raises optimism, but he deferred to the injury report and said they would see how the week goes. Kyle Hamilton and a few others missed practice with what Minter called typical after-game soreness, and he felt pretty good about them. The right guard spot is described as open between Andrew Vorhees (no longer on the injury report) and Emery Jones, with the best player to start. Next up is Buffalo, which Minter said has leaned into a physical three-tight-end running game, play action and boots, with Josh Allen acting as an extra runner and extending plays. Minter said the run defense needed work, which was part of why they wore pads, and he stressed tackling and four-quarter focus. He praised safeties K'Von Wallace and Keondre Jackson for their energy in the last game and said he is excited about new defensive back Jaylinn Hawkins, who has position flexibility across big nickel, dime and safety. He also said that with three games now missing Jackson, others have stepped up at times and at times not, and that everyone in the building needs to do more.

injuries.detail: Got some work in at Wednesday practice; Minter was optimistic but deferred to the injury report and said they'd see how the week goes.
Did not practice Wednesday; Minter described it as typical after-game soreness for a few players and felt pretty good about it.
Not on the injury report; Minter said they'd see where he is after a week of practice, praising his mentality.

signals.claim: Jackson's availability for Sunday will depend on how he responds through the week of practice; no confirmation he will play.
signals.note: Optimistic tone but no commitment; monitor Thursday and Friday injury reports before locking in lineups.

signals.claim: Vorhees is competing with Emery Jones for the starting right guard job this week.
signals.note: Right guard is an open competition, which matters slightly for Baltimore's run game and pass protection.
signals.quote: I think it's open.

signals.claim: Jones is competing with Vorhees for the starting right guard job this week.
signals.note: Jones could keep the right guard job if Vorhees is not ready.
signals.quote: we'll put the best guy out there that we feel gives us the best opportunity

signals.claim: Hamilton missed Wednesday's practice with minor after-game issues and his status will be clarified as the week goes on.
signals.note: Key IDP safety; worth tracking his practice participation later in the week.

signals.claim: Wallace played well in his opportunity last game and remains in the safety mix.
signals.note: Could keep a role in the secondary, a small IDP bump.
signals.quote: I give Kavon a lot of credit.

signals.claim: Jackson played well in his opportunity last game and remains in the safety mix.
signals.note: Could keep a role in the secondary, a small IDP bump.

signals.claim: Hawkins, newly added, will be worked into the defensive back mix with versatility across big nickel, dime and safety.
signals.note: A new arrival who could cut into safety snaps, which matters for IDP formats.
signals.quote: he's got position flexibility

topics.detail: Buffalo is running more of a physical, big-bodied ground game with two or three tight ends, which sets up play action and boot concepts for Josh Allen. Minter expects the defense to be defending an extra runner in Allen and extended scramble plays.

Baltimore practiced in pads partly to prepare for Buffalo's run game and with a short week coming next. Minter emphasized tackling, sustained four-quarter effort and an us-against-the-world mentality after a loss, and took accountability for play calls and fourth-down decisions.

title: Joe Brady On Improvements After The Bye Week
headline: DJ Moore is expected back at practice today after missing games, Tyrell Shavers is being activated, and Ed Oliver returns to practice, while C.J. Gardner-Johnson is out this week.
summary: Brady said the Bills are back from the bye with a full week of practice to clean up technique and details, and he stressed that a reset is useful for the offense as well as the defense. He said DJ Moore should be back on the field today after sitting out games, and called Moore tough and a playmaker the offense needs. Tyrell Shavers will be activated and practice today, and Brady praised his mindset after an ACL tear, though he framed him mostly as a special teams and culture player. Jordan Hancock is eligible to come off IR but will not practice today, and the team will keep evaluating him. Ed Oliver will practice today; Brady said the defensive line has played well without him and that his return helps the defense. He called Keon Coleman reliable, smart and versatile, and said he needs to keep getting opportunities. Brady also said Gardner-Johnson will not be available this week, and that Tre'Davious White was re-signed as veteran secondary depth with no guaranteed role. Next up is Baltimore, with Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry described as a big task. He also defended Sam Franklin, who is back this week after a suspension he considers unjustified.

injuries.detail: Missed recent games; Brady said it would be nice to get him back on the field today and see how it goes.
Eligible to return from IR this week but won't practice today; the team will keep evaluating him.
Per a reporter's question, he won't be available this week; Brady did not dispute it.
Has missed about half the games; he will be out at practice today.
Opening his practice window and activating today after ACL recovery.

signals.claim: DJ Moore will return to practice today and could be back in the lineup against Baltimore.
signals.note: A healthy Moore adds a playmaking target to the passing game and may cut into other WRs' targets.
signals.quote: it'd be nice to get him back on the football field today

signals.claim: Keon Coleman will keep getting opportunities and will be moved around the offense.
signals.note: Brady's praise of his reliability and the trust from Josh Allen point to a stable role in the passing game.
signals.quote: He's one of our smartest football players, right? He's as smart as they come.

signals.claim: Shavers will be activated and practice today, and he is expected to contribute on special teams.
signals.note: Brady spoke of him as a special teams and culture player who doesn't care about catches, so his fantasy value is limited.
signals.quote: doesn't give a damn about if he has a catch

signals.claim: Ed Oliver will practice today and is expected to help the defense as he returns.
signals.note: His return improves the Bills' defensive line and could help IDP and defense matchups.

signals.claim: Hancock will not practice today and the team will continue evaluating him.
signals.note: He is IR-eligible, but Brady gave no timeline for his return.
signals.quote: We'll continue to kind of evaluate him.

signals.claim: Gardner-Johnson will not play this week.
signals.note: The safety group stays thin for the Baltimore game, which matters for IDP and defense streaming.

topics.detail: Brady called Lamar Jackson one of the best players in the world and Derrick Henry another Hall of Famer. He said Baltimore is two-dimensional and will be a huge task for the defense.
Brady wants players to trust the system and each other rather than trying to be heroes, and wants better tackling and more takeaways. He declined to single out the safeties.
He was brought back as veteran secondary depth because of injuries, will work on special teams first, and has no guaranteed role.
The Bills reviewed tape in each room and focused on on-schedule versus off-schedule results and third-and-long and third-and-medium situations.
Brady praised the special teams unit, led by Coach Rogers, as the team's ethos.
Brady defended Franklin against accusations he said lacked evidence, and said Franklin will be available this week.

title: Ben Johnson previews Monday night matchup in Seattle | Press Conference
headline: Daniel Hardy is in line for more defensive snaps, Caleb Williams is getting the ball out on rhythm, and Montez Sweat is back and may see more one-on-ones in Seattle.
summary: Johnson called Seattle, the defending champion, a really well-coached team with talent in all three phases, and said Monday night on the road will be a big test. He praised their pass rush, which gets home with four rushers, and their ability to take away explosive plays and get off the field. He said Chicago has to stop the penalties and protect the football. He thinks Caleb Williams is playing slightly more on time and on rhythm. He credited that to extensive reps with the concepts and a consistent staff approach, and said Williams is self-critical and handles that well. On defense, Montez Sweat is back after missing a couple of games and has been steady against the run. Johnson wants more pass-rush impact from him and hopes the pressure packages of Daniel Hardy and Austin Booker get Sweat more one-on-one looks. Hardy was singled out for deserving more playing time. A player the captions render as 'Colby/Kobe' is on track in a knee rehab but is still weeks from change-of-direction work, and Johnson kept his return timeline vague. Johnson also said general manager Ryan Poles is handling trade-deadline work, and that he himself sees big room for improvement in the run and pass games after a self-scout.

injuries.detail: Back in the lineup after missing a couple of games. Johnson did not describe any limitation.

Knee rehab is on track. He will soon start on-land running but is still a ways from change-of-direction work. Johnson would not narrow the earlier mid-December to February window, saying the next month will show whether he returns this year.

signals.claim: Williams will keep getting the ball out on time and in rhythm, with continued improvement in accuracy on run-after-catch throws.
signals.note: Faster, more rhythmic quarterback play helps the pass catchers, though Seattle's pass defense is a tough matchup.
signals.quote: just a tick more of him playing on time and on rhythm

signals.claim: Hardy will get more defensive snaps after being the team's best pass rusher over the last two weeks.
signals.note: A growing edge role matters for IDP and pass-rush-based fantasy formats.
signals.quote: a guy that certainly warrants a little bit more playing time on defense as well.

signals.claim: Chicago hopes to get Sweat more one-on-one pass-rush chances through the pressure packages and the other rushers.
signals.note: He has been solid against the run but his pass-rush production has been modest, and he is being challenged to improve it.
signals.quote: he's been kind of a steady Eddie guy for us

signals.claim: Booker's pass-rush impact is part of a rotation that should free Sweat for more one-on-one matchups.
signals.note: He is productive getting to the quarterback and is likely to keep a meaningful pass-rush role.
signals.quote: Booker's impact getting to the quarterback

signals.note: Johnson gave a lukewarm evaluation and tied playing time to weekly performance, so his role is worth watching.
signals.quote: there's been some ups and downs.

topics.detail: Johnson said Seattle affects the quarterback with only four rushers and takes away explosive plays. They force offenses to sustain drives, and their tape shows a lot of three-and-outs. He said it will take a team effort.

After the extra time, Johnson said the staff checked formation and run/pass numbers. He said there is a lot of room to improve in both the run and pass games, and he will do a deeper dive at the bye week.
Johnson said recent penalties have been costly and must stop on the road. He stressed taking care of the football.

He said Seattle's offense runs through its lead receiver, who gets double-digit targets nearly every week. He said the run game is a focus after their trade and that he will watch whether their runners are healthy.
Johnson said roster moves are Ryan Poles's domain, with constant dialogue about the team's needs. He said Poles is turning over every stone.

opponent: Seattle Seahawks (Monday night, on the road)

title: Zac Taylor: "This Is A Tremendous Opportunity" | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Erick All is done for the year with a torn ACL, Tanner Hudson is week-to-week with a quad injury, and rookie TE Jack Endries is in line for a bigger role. Chase Brown is still the featured back.
summary: Zac Taylor confirmed that Erick All tore his ACL, his third, and said the team will support him through rehab. He said Tanner Hudson's quad injury is week-to-week. With both tight ends out, Taylor said other tight ends will have to pick up the slack. He singled out drafted rookie Jack Endries, saying he has earned the opportunity and that he isn't nervous about using him. Taylor said PJ Jules and Russ Yeast are trusted safety depth. On Chase Brown, who has no explosive run yet, he said the team counts on him in a big way and nobody needs to press. He said the two-back looks used situationally this year depend on the game and matchups, and will be reassessed weekly. He credited the red zone offense's success to heavy preparation, on-time throws and players executing complex calls. He said he feels great about the roster despite trade-deadline noise. The team is home this week against Tennessee after a month away, and Taylor wants to use the crowd noise. He called Tennessee's offense dangerous and singled out Tony Pollard. He also praised Titans DT Jeffery Simmons as arguably among the top defensive linemen.

injuries.detail: Tore his ACL, the third time. Taylor said the team will support his rehab, so he is effectively out for the season.
Quad injury described as week-to-week, with no firm timeline.

signals.claim: Will miss the rest of the season with a torn ACL.
signals.note: He is off the fantasy radar for the year, which thins the Bengals' tight end room.
signals.quote: He tore his ACL, so it's awful for him.

signals.claim: Will be week-to-week with a quad injury and may miss time.
signals.note: Hudson has been a red zone target, so his absence opens tight end targets for others.

signals.claim: Will step into a larger tight end role with All and Hudson hurt.
signals.note: The rookie tight end is a streaming or deep-league pickup with a clear path to snaps.
signals.quote: I'm not nervous at all about using him. I think he's earned the opportunity.

signals.claim: Will remain a heavily relied-upon back in the offense.
signals.note: Taylor expressed confidence and no concern about the lack of explosive runs, so his workload looks safe.
signals.quote: I love his approach.

signals.claim: Will continue as safety depth when needed.
signals.note: Only relevant for IDP leagues, and only if a safety injury forces him into the lineup.
signals.quote: I feel very confident in PJ and Russ.

signals.claim: Will continue as safety depth when needed.
signals.note: Only relevant for IDP leagues, and only if a safety injury forces him into the lineup.
signals.quote: I feel very confident in PJ and Russ.

topics.detail: The team has used two running backs together situationally, on both first and passing downs. Taylor said it depends on the game and matchups, and the team will reassess weekly.
Taylor credited heavy weekly preparation, recycled plays that weren't called earlier, and on-time throws rather than scrambles. He cited TDs to Tanner (Hudson) against Miami and Mike Gesicki.
Asked about under-center usage, Taylor said it changes week to week.
Taylor called Tony Pollard a big weapon under Brian Daboll's offense, praised rookie QB Cam Ward's growth, and said Jeffery Simmons is arguably among the top defensive linemen.
Taylor said he feels great about the roster and dismissed trade rumors as made up. He is looking forward to the Paycor Stadium crowd noise after a month away.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference - October 28th, 2026
headline: Monken doesn't expect an unnamed player's knee swelling to cost him Sunday at Pittsburgh. He expects Dylan Sampson to improve in his second game back, and KC Concepcion's touches are "critical."
summary: Monken spent most of the session downplaying the Steelers rivalry and the 22-game road losing streak in Pittsburgh. He said only this week's preparation matters, and that a divisional game is the fastest way into the playoffs. He praised the offense's two-minute work and Deshaun Watson's late-game play, crediting protection, skill players and situational understanding. He said he'd prefer Watson run as little as possible. He saw a "baby step" in the run game against Baltimore and better results last week on rundowns. A player who wasn't practicing with a knee issue (name not captured in the transcript) has only minor swelling, and Monken doesn't anticipate it keeping him out Sunday. He expects Dylan Sampson to be a better version of himself this week after he was rusty in his first game back from roughly five to six weeks out. He called KC Concepcion quick, powerful and tough, and said getting him the ball is critical. He described the offense as "under construction" and up and down. On the Steelers, he praised Aaron Rodgers (accuracy, quick release, operation) and Patrick Graham's mix of pressures and ball-batting.

injuries.detail: Did not practice Wednesday because of a knee. Monken said it's just a little swelling, they wanted to keep him off it, and he doesn't anticipate it keeping him out Sunday.
Played his first game back last week after about five to six weeks out. Monken said he looked like a shell of himself and expects him to be better this week and next.

signals.claim: Sampson will look better and be more effective in his second game back, and is used as an explosive player in space.
signals.note: Monken expects Sampson to shake off the rust, which could mean a bigger role in the offense in the coming weeks.
signals.quote: I expect him to be even a better version of himself this week

signals.claim: The offense will keep looking for ways to get Concepcion the ball.
signals.note: Monken singled him out as a priority touch-getter who can score every time he touches it.
signals.quote: finding ways to get him the ball is obviously critical to our offense

signals.claim: Watson's rushing attempts should stay low if the run game keeps being efficient, as it was against Tennessee.
signals.note: Coach wants to reduce reliance on Watson's legs, which could cap his rushing production while the passing and two-minute work stays strong.
signals.quote: give yourself a chance to take the pressure off the quarterback

topics.detail: Cleveland travels to Pittsburgh for a divisional game Sunday. Monken stressed the rivalry and history don't matter and that the focus is Wednesday's practice. He praised Patrick Graham's pressure mixing, including interior pressures, and the Steelers' edge rushers batting down balls.
Monken called the offense up and down and "always under construction." He saw a baby step against Baltimore and better rundown efficiency last week, which let them call the game more comfortably.

Monken said a reserve who has had to play significant snaps off the bench did well and has worked harder and been more diligent in practice recently. The name was garbled in the transcript (possibly Dawand Jones, but not certain), so no signal was assigned.

Monken called Rodgers a first-ballot Hall of Famer and said Cleveland needs to build leads against him. He also said Watson and the offense have found a way to succeed in two-minute situations this season.

title: HC Sean Payton on home-field advantage in Week 8: ‘In a game like this, it’s significant’
headline: Payton says Marvin Mims Jr. deserves more touches but personnel and coverage limit it; Pat Bryant and Jaylen Waddle are banged up, and Denver's run game is improving ahead of a Week 8 divisional game against Kansas City.
summary: Payton previewed the Week 8 divisional game against the Chiefs, noting Kansas City has committed more to the run and added a runner. He said Denver is studying crossover film, including how Seattle's defense handled them, though only some of it carries over. He praised Alex Singleton, the Defensive Player of the Week, for his instincts and run-game plays. He said Marvin Mims Jr. keeps producing as a receiver and returner and is deserving of more touches, but coverage and personnel groupings get in the way. When asked about injured receivers he named Pat Bryant and Waddle, with no specifics on their status. He said the run game took a step last week, but this week's front is different and the focus shifts to technique against the ends. He explained that road games are harder for Bo Nix and the center because of silent counts, and said Denver's home crowd noise has been significant. He also broke down Nix's 62-yard touchdown run as a read against match coverage, and praised Malcolm Roach and Nik Bonitto. He also said winning the division is not dependent on this game, though it would make things easier.

injuries.detail: Named by a reporter as banged up; Payton gave no specific status, only that practice was good.
Named alongside Bryant as banged up; Payton gave no timeline or practice details.

signals.claim: Mims will keep getting touches, and Denver hopes to find more opportunities for him through personnel groupings.
signals.note: Payton called him deserving of more touches but admitted coverage and a crowded healthy receiver room limit his volume, so a big target jump is not guaranteed.
signals.quote: certainly he's, he's deserving.

signals.claim: Singleton will continue to play a major role in the defense, especially against the run.
signals.note: He is coming off a Defensive Player of the Week performance, which is useful for IDP managers.
signals.quote: he's playing well with good instincts

signals.claim: Nix's running and pre-snap communication will matter in a loud road environment, and he made a good read on his 62-yard TD run.
signals.note: His scrambling is partly a function of scheme (match coverage keeps eyes on receivers), so it may not be a repeatable rushing floor.
signals.quote: he did a good job of just sensing a cavity.

signals.claim: Bonitto's pass-rush pressure is valued even when it doesn't result in sacks.
signals.note: Payton praised his instincts and get-off, though the praise is about pressure rather than sack totals.
signals.quote: he's he's got real good instincts.

signals.claim: Roach is a reliable, consistent defensive lineman who has grown into more of a pass-rush role.
signals.note: Mild positive for IDP managers; Payton spoke more about reliability than production.
signals.quote: you know exactly what you're getting.

signals.claim: Bryant is among the receivers banged up this week.
signals.note: Payton did not specify severity, so monitor practice reports.

signals.claim: Waddle is among the receivers banged up this week.
signals.note: Payton did not specify severity, so monitor practice reports.

topics.detail: Payton said the run game took a step forward last week but the opposing front differs from recent games, so the focus is on technique against the ends.

He noted Kansas City is more committed to the run this year with the addition of a runner. Denver is studying film from multiple seasons and from how others defended them, including Seattle and Indianapolis.
Silent counts on the road burden Nix and the center, and Denver's loud home stadium adds stress for opponents. Payton called the crowd effect significant in a game like this.
He said this game is not a must-win for the division title but would make it easier. The team's goals are the division, then playoff seed, then a championship.
Payton praised Travis Kelce's instincts, ability to feel coverage and sudden transitions out of breaks.
Asked about the trade deadline, Payton gave no specifics and said George Paton watches it and they would discuss it.

title: Campbell on Vikings defense
headline: Kerby Joseph's practice clock starts this week as he returns from knee surgery, while the Lions prepare for Minnesota's 6-0 blitz-heavy defense.
summary: Campbell opened by saying Ennis Rakestraw is doing well but will be held out of practice. A couple of other players were also held back to rest their legs, and the team will do a walk-through before practice. Safety Kerby Joseph's practice clock starts today after he passed every strength and swelling test. He will progress week by week, with contact-style football reps likely late this week or early next week. Campbell called the 6-0 Vikings an excellent, veteran defense under Brian Flores that forces turnovers and big mistakes, so he stressed poise and patience on offense. He also said the Lions' defense has to keep up its recent level of play against Kyler Murray's mobility and a dangerous skill group. He praised Jared Goff's poise and quick processing against the blitz and called this a great strength-on-strength matchup. He also gave a long explanation of his aggressive fourth-down philosophy, saying it comes from belief and feel for each week's matchup rather than analytics.

injuries.detail: Knee/quad rehab. His practice clock starts today with individual work. He has passed all strength and swelling tests, and contact-style football reps are expected late this week or early next week.
Campbell said he's doing good but will be held out of the practice portion, though he is in the walk-through. No injury was specified.

signals.claim: Joseph will be gradually ramped up and move into real football-contact reps late this week or early next week.
signals.note: He is trending toward a return to the Lions' secondary, which matters for IDP and defensive matchup context, but there is still no firm game date.
signals.quote: he's passed every test to this point.

signals.claim: Goff will handle Minnesota's heavy blitz pressure with quick diagnosis and good decisions.
signals.note: Campbell is confident in Goff against a pressure-heavy defense, though the Vikings forced Detroit turnovers last year.
signals.quote: He's very poised. He's very smart and he knows his issues.

topics.detail: Campbell called Minnesota's defense 'as good as it gets': veteran, versatile and well-schooled in Flores's system. He said it exploits offenses, takes away their outlets, and forces turnovers and big mistakes. His plan is poise and patience, avoiding third-and-long.

He said Kyler Murray can extend plays and drives with his legs and facilitates well. He also praised Justin Jefferson, T.J. Hockenson's recent production, Jordan Mason's downhill running and the special teams. The Lions' defense has to keep up its play of the last two weeks.

Campbell said he doesn't study fourth-down analytics much. He goes by feel for the week's matchup and personnel, favors going on short yardage in the red zone, and cited Sean Payton's influence. He is comfortable with last week's failed attempt.

He framed the matchup history as a team-wide cat-and-mouse game, said Minnesota did a great job against Detroit last year, and said the Lions must play much better, especially in taking care of the ball.

title: Shane Steichen: Midweek update, Colts at Jaguars
headline: Colts traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner; Steichen says young linemen (Jalen Farmer, 'Tommy') must step up, QB depth chart unchanged, and Cam Taylor-Britt is out a while but not season-ending.
summary: Steichen opened by praising Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner and acknowledged both trades were tough, but said the focus is now on preparing for the Jaguars on the road. He said he didn't sugarcoat the message to the team: it's a business, young players must step up, and the team needs to improve every day. He declined to say whether either player requested a trade and wouldn't address whether Jonathan Taylor asked to be traded, calling it hypothetical, though he said JT is on the team. The team is 2-5, but Steichen said expectations are unchanged and he has been on teams that rallied from similar starts. He confirmed the quarterback depth chart hasn't changed. The team did a walkthrough instead of a practice to keep players fresh because Jacksonville is coming off a bye, and he said it was his idea. At cornerback, he deferred to the injury report, said several players are banged up, praised Kenneth Harris's Week 7 play and practice work, and said Cam Taylor-Britt will be out for a bit but it likely isn't season-ending. He also praised Jalen Farmer's work ethic as he steps into Nelson's spot, and complimented a young defensive lineman referred to as 'Tommy' (name unclear in captions) for his effort and growth.

title: Liam Coen on Prep for Divisional Matchup vs. Colts, Getting Back on Track | Press Conference
headline: Jaguars (4-2) return from the bye to host the Colts; Montaric Brown and Antonio Johnson did light work on Monday, and Brian Thomas Jr. is expected to bounce back but his targets depend on performance.
summary: Coach Coen played down the Colts' trade-deadline moves, saying the focus is on the Jaguars' own execution, fundamentals and getting back on track after the loss to Houston. He praised Indianapolis, noting Daniel Jones is moving well, throwing from the pocket and on the move, and still pushing the ball downfield. He expects Tyler Warren back and said much of the Colts' offense runs through him, and he respects Jonathan Taylor and their run schemes. Coen credited the Jaguars' third-down success to repeating core concepts and banked reps from the offseason and camp. He said the pass rush has to improve and needs help from the back end and second level, but he still has faith in the group. On Brian Thomas Jr.'s slow stretch, he said he fully expects him to make plays Sunday, though he also said he will go with the hot hand and that roles and targets depend on performance. Montaric Brown and Antonio Johnson did a little work with the training staff on Monday and will be evaluated again today. Coen said a healthier Brown would be a huge boost to the secondary. He expects a tight, physical game with contested catches and possible weather, and he said the offense has scored over 30 in both home games, partly thanks to easier communication.

injuries.detail: Did a little on the grass with the training staff Monday; Coen said they would see more today. A healthier Brown is 'huge' for the secondary.
Did a little on the grass with the training staff Monday alongside Brown; more will be known at today's practice.

signals.claim: Will make plays against the Colts on Sunday, but his reps and targets depend on performance and who has the hot hand.
signals.note: Coen backed him publicly but did not promise volume, so treat his role as performance-dependent.
signals.quote: I fully anticipate he's going to make plays for us this Sunday.

signals.claim: Brown is working his way back and would strengthen the defense if healthy.
signals.note: His return would stabilize the secondary and may affect how opposing passing games are defended.
signals.quote: Huge.

signals.note: His availability for Sunday is still open and depends on practice participation this week.
signals.quote: Buster Antonio did just a little bit buzzed around with the training staff.

topics.detail: Coen said Daniel Jones is moving well, throwing from the pocket and on the move, and still pushing the ball downfield. He expects Tyler Warren back this week and called Jonathan Taylor a high-level back with strong run schemes and tight ends who block well.

Indianapolis has good corners who play man and challenge receivers, and Lou Anarumo mixes single-high match coverage with two-high looks. Coen expects tough contested catches, possibly in bad weather.
Coen said he tries not to think about it, calling it 'rat poison.' He said the Jaguars are preparing for a competitive game and assume the Colts will play loose.
Coen attributed it to running core concepts repeatedly instead of overcomplicating them, plus offseason and camp reps.

The rush needs better hand usage, matchups and pressure looks, plus help from the coverage behind it. Coen said the communication problems against Houston came from chasing the game after falling behind early.
The offense has scored 30+ in both home games, which Coen attributes largely to easier communication. He said the team has not discussed the Colts' streak in Jacksonville.

title: Andy Reid: 'Look Forward to the Challenge of Playing the Broncos' | Press Conference 10/28
headline: Cyrus Allen's WR role is growing again this week, while Andy Reid says all players will practice Wednesday and Justin Tucker joins the practice squad to push Harrison Butker (Bud/Booker in captions).
summary: Reid opened by saying everybody will practice Wednesday, so there are no injury concerns to report ahead of a road game against a good Denver team. Most of the questions were about the kicker situation. The Chiefs signed Justin Tucker to the practice squad after Harrison Butker struggled, including in the loss at Seattle. Reid said Tucker served his suspension and impressed in a three-man workout. He said Butker's technique is off and inconsistent, and that Butker will get most of the reps this week and will probably play. Reid hasn't seen a scenario with both kickers active. On the offense, he admitted the pass protection must improve after Seattle's pressure package, and said the drop in snaps under center came from needing to throw in the second half after falling behind. He said Cyrus Allen is being grown into the offense and will get a bit more work than last week. On Denver, Reid said they've added Cooper back, who looks full go, and that they are fast, talented and improved every week. He gave a general answer about what it takes for a receiver to learn quickly if the team adds one, without naming any player.

injuries.detail: Reid said everybody will practice Wednesday; no injuries were listed.

signals.claim: Allen will get a few more offensive snaps this week than last week.
signals.note: His role is trending up, which makes him a speculative WR add or watch, although the increase is small.

Snaps under center fell to a season low because the Chiefs needed to throw more in the second half while trailing by a couple of scores. Reid said he isn't for or against the approach.
Denver is a talented, fast and improving team with a good front. Cooper is back and appears full go, and the Chiefs have to be prepared on the road.
Reid spoke generally about incoming receivers needing to learn the offense quickly and have the aptitude to jump in midseason. He named no one.

title: Sean McVay & Matthew Stafford discuss mentality and preparation ahead of matchup against the Chargers in Week 8
headline: Davante Adams' surgery went well and the projected return is on the shorter end of 6-10 weeks. Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson remain week-to-week with their clocks not started, and TE Colby Parkinson is a DNP (rib).
summary: McVay opened with the Wednesday injury report. Coleman Shelton (hip), Colby Parkinson (rib) and long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle) were DNP, Trent McDuffie was limited, and Nathan Landman and Desjuan Johnson were full. The team will not start the practice-window clock for Myles Garrett or Terrance Ferguson this week. McVay said Garrett is making good progress and is week to week, with no setback and no further procedure that he knows of. He said Davante Adams' surgery went well and the timeline is probably closer to the shorter end of a 6-10 week range. The Rams added long snapper Jake McQuaide as a contingency for Cardona, brought kicker Josh Carty back, and signed John Ratkin for special-teams value. McVay called the winless Chargers a really good, well-coached team that is getting healthy on offense, and said the Rams have their hands full. On the trade deadline, he said he expects injured key players to return rather than chasing trades. The second half of the transcript is Matthew Stafford speaking, not McVay.

title: Jim Harbaugh on Offensive Adjustments Following the Bye Week
headline: Derwin James had a rehab setback and may go to IR. Joe Alt's return is called a 'big boost' for the line, and Ladd McConkey is expected to practice from the concussion protocol.

Brenen Thompson won't practice, Deane Leonard is still in the concussion protocol, and Khalil Mack gets a rest day. Ladd McConkey is also in the protocol but is expected to practice, and Tre Harris is believed to be practicing, though he is not quite eligible for IR activation. Most of the rest of the session was about a bye-week deep dive into the offense, which he said covered every phase and the whole organization, not just the offense. He framed the goal as efficiency and getting 'a percent better' in every situation, from normal downs to the red zone and two-minute work. Players had input through position meetings, unit meetings and an open-mic format. Harbaugh repeatedly backed OC Mike McDaniel, said he was familiar with the system when he hired him, and said he trusts McDaniel and the position coaches. He did not give specific scheme changes. He said Joe Alt's potential return would be a big boost. Reporters pressed on the team's poor start, but he stayed general and said the focus is to 'win the day'.

title: Klint Kubiak details position battles ahead of Week 8 vs. Jets
headline: Jack Bech (listed as 'Bash' in captions) could return for Week 8 vs. the Jets, Mike Washington Jr. is back to practicing and 'looks like his old self,' and Trey Zuhn will keep cross-training across the O-line as Kubiak shakes up the line.
summary: Kubiak opened by saying Patrick Johnson did not practice and Kwity Paye was limited with what he called a rest day. He deflected questions about the run game, saying the issues are a team-wide problem rather than the fault of any one player, and said the offense needs to run the ball better and 'quit throwing it so much.' He praised rookie Trey Zuhn as a Swiss Army knife who can play tackle, guard or center and said he will keep playing multiple positions while the staff keeps shaking up the line until it finds the right mix. Kubiak said he believes Jack Bech has a chance to be ready Sunday, praising his energy and run blocking, though he credited the current blocking receivers too. Dont'e Thornton Jr. is working hard to come back and is competing for a job, and Kubiak said he must beat out another receiver to take that spot. Mike Washington Jr. practiced and looks like his old self after playing banged up on Sunday. Kubiak said the team is 3-4 with plenty of season left, called the Jets physical, talented and well coached, and said run defense problems come down to tackling, alignment and assignment. He also said Kirk Cousins is consistent and productive, and that the front office is talking daily about trades near the deadline.

title: Kevin O’Connell on Blake Cashman, Looking Ahead to the Lions, Injury Updates & Being 6-0
headline: Aaron Jones (day-to-day) and OL Joe Huber (knee soreness) sat out Wednesday's practice but O'Connell sounds optimistic about both for the Week 8 game at Detroit; he says the offense will keep trying to get Justin Jefferson the ball.
summary: O'Connell opened by praising Blake Cashman, the NFC Defensive Player of the Week, for leading the defense as the green dot. He called the divisional road game at Detroit a major challenge against a talented, well-coached team with momentum, and said the Vikings (6-0) will need their best game yet. For injuries, Aaron Jones and Joe Huber did not practice Wednesday. Huber had knee soreness pop up after the game and O'Connell is not overly worried, while Jones is day-to-day and feels strong. Guards Trevor Keegan and Caleb Tiernan are taking extra snaps as a contingency plan while Huber is out. On the trade deadline, he said Nolan and his staff are continuing to evaluate opportunities and will act if something makes sense, with no firm commitment. On Justin Jefferson's modest production, he cited a run-heavy early-down approach, split-safety looks from opponents like the Colts, and missed opportunities, and he said production should come in bunches for Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson. He also said the offense needs to run the ball, marry the run and pass, generate explosives and avoid turnovers, and he praised Kyler Murray's legs and off-schedule plays.

He said the team will keep weighing whether TreVeyon Henderson goes back to returning kicks, but the return game will be worked on with Corey Kiner or Kyle Williams and others considered. Harrison Phillips and Demario Davis have rest days, and Breece Hall, Dylan Parham and Braelon Allen (ankle) are limited. Glenn praised Allen's growth as a receiver: he has hit career highs in receiving yards two games running, gets a good route tree, and is sometimes split out in empty sets. signals.quote: the role won't change.

signals.claim: Hall is limited in practice Wednesday and is being brought back.
signals.note: He is practicing but limited, so his game availability depends on the rest of the week.

signals.claim: Taylor will keep being used as a contested-catch and run-after-catch target.
signals.note: The coach highlighted his high-point catches and improved blocking, which supports a steady tight end role.
signals.quote: his blocking is really improving.

signals.note: Glenn praised Cooper's current play, a good sign for his standing in the receiver group.
signals.quote: he's doing a hell of a job for us

topics.detail: Glenn called the Raiders a talented team in all three phases. He singled out Max Crosby's disruption on defense, Brock Bowers as a receiver/tight end hybrid to be careful with, and Tucker as a deep threat who opens the middle for Bowers. He also noted that the two Raiders running backs have different styles.
Glenn said Cousins looks healthy after the Achilles injury and processes at an elite level. The Jets plan to change coverages so he can't get a beat on them.

Glenn pointed to the margins: red-zone offense and defense on second-and-long. He said the Jets are putting more practice time into two-minute offense and defense after struggling in games, and that it starts with him.
Asked whether calling the defense is stretching him thin, Glenn said it isn't easy but he'll put the stress on himself. He credited Duke with helping him study the offense and install the defense.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 28, 2026
headline: Joe Milton II has leapfrogged Cole Payton for the No. 2 QB job, Makai Lemon and Eli Stowers are on the rise, and Sirianni flagged offensive line and run-game progress after the loss to Dallas.
summary: Sirianni opened by praising rookie tackle Markel Bell, saying Monday night was his best game of the year and that his toughness and love of football point to continued growth. He denied there was an effort problem in the loss to the Cowboys, saying the team grades alignment, assignment and effort on every play and that the issues were elsewhere. He took responsibility for the defensive struggles, including the lack of pass-rush impact and the run defense giving up many yards, but would not get into scheme. He said that blitzing against Dallas's playmakers means leaving more defenders in coverage. On the quarterback room, he said Joe Milton II moved up to the No. 2 spot because of good practices and developmental reps, and stressed that the team still believes in Cole Payton, who is the third QB and still developing. He praised rookies Makai Lemon, Eli Stowers (getting back and starting to get run) and Keyshawn James-Newby (contributing on special teams and some defense). He said the offensive line played solid and created running lanes with good protection until the team had to abandon balance late while down two possessions. He added that the offense installed a couple of new things and has a lot to build on. He declined to discuss hypotheticals about players being traded, saying only that he would support any player privately, and he pushed back on the idea that the team is in a poor place, citing a five-game losing streak and process over outcome.

injuries.detail: Sirianni said Stowers is 'getting back' and starting to get some run, implying he is returning from a prior absence.

signals.claim: Joe Milton II is now the team's No. 2 quarterback ahead of Cole Payton.
signals.note: He is now the next man up behind Jalen Hurts, which matters for handcuff value only if Hurts is hurt.
signals.quote: Joe's have has a little bit more experience

signals.claim: Cole Payton is the third QB for now while he continues to develop.
signals.note: He is no longer the top backup, so he has little fantasy relevance.
signals.quote: we do believe in coal. And coal has been the third.

signals.claim: Makai Lemon has shown growth as a rookie and is expected to keep developing into a good player.
signals.note: Strong praise from the coach suggests he could hold or expand his role in the passing game.
signals.quote: I think we've all seen the growth of Makai Lemon

signals.claim: Eli Stowers is returning and getting more snaps as his playing time increases.
signals.note: A returning rookie tight end getting reps is worth monitoring as his role grows.
signals.quote: Eli getting back and and starting to get some, uh, run

signals.claim: James-Newby will keep contributing on special teams and in some defensive snaps.
signals.note: A limited role means little for IDP value unless his defensive snaps increase.

signals.claim: Bell is improving and played his best game of the year on Monday night.
signals.note: Better tackle play helps pass protection and the running game, with spillover value for Eagles skill players.
signals.quote: I think he played his best game of the year

signals.claim: Dickerson was back in the lineup and the offensive line played solidly with him.
signals.note: A healthy line is good for the run game and for Saquon Barkley and Jalen Hurts.

topics.detail: Sirianni took responsibility for the pass rush and run defense issues, saying blitzing against Dallas's playmakers means leaving more defenders in coverage, and he refused to discuss scheme.
He rejected the narrative that effort was an issue, saying the film grades effort on every play and that he grades objectively rather than by the result.

The line created running lanes and protected well through three-plus quarters, and a no-huddle approach late forced the offense away from its designed balance. Some new additions to the offense were installed.
He declined to discuss hypothetical trades of players and stressed supporting players personally and professionally.
Facing a five-game losing streak, he compared the situation to 2021 and emphasized a daily process, with no shortcuts.

title: WATCH: Mike McCarthy Media Availability (Oct. 28)
headline: Roman Wilson won't be ready this week, and the Steelers face an aggressive Browns defense that wins with its four-man rush; Zach Frazier and the O-line got high praise.
summary: McCarthy described the Browns defense as aggressive and gap-based, with a four-man rush, an improved stunt game, and veteran corners who play bump-and-run. On offense he said Cleveland gets the ball to its perimeter players, who break tackles, and that the Browns have won a lot of fourth-quarter games. He said the team's energy is good after a long travel stretch, and the Steelers are using Wednesday to get their legs back. A player named Deshaun, who played about 20 snaps in the first game back after roughly a year, looks good. McCarthy would not commit to a bigger workload for him and said the week of preparation will answer that. He said Roman Wilson won't be ready this week. He praised center Zach Frazier as having a great year, with strong leadership, preparation, physicality and leverage. He also said the O-line is growing because the same five get to practice and play together. He closed by saying the team's run of one-possession games is good training for the playoffs.

injuries.detail: McCarthy said he won't be ready this week; no further timeline given.

signals.claim: Will not return to the field for the Week 8 game against the Browns.
signals.note: Wilson is unavailable this week, so he has no fantasy value in the short term.
signals.quote: he won't be ready this week.

signals.note: A strong, improving center and O-line helps the run game and pass protection, which supports the Steelers' skill players.
signals.quote: Zach Frazier is having a great year.

topics.detail: McCarthy called it an aggressive gap defense with a good four-man rush, an improved stunt game, and veteran corners playing bump-and-run techniques that fit their skill set.
Cleveland spreads the ball to perimeter players who break tackles, and it has won a lot of games in the fourth quarter.
McCarthy said the line is growing and has been part of the offense's success. Continuity from the same five practicing and playing together helps both run blocking and pass protection.
The team came out of the travel stretch with good energy. Wednesday's practice was meant to let players recover, with positive weight room and conditioning work.
The Steelers have played an unusual number of one-possession games. McCarthy said the team trains for those situations and they prepare it for the playoffs.

title: Todd Bowles on Staying Aggressive on Defense | Press Conference
headline: Bucky Irving is the 'bell cow' RB, Ted Hurst is trending up, and Luke Goedeke's Sunday availability looks slim, while Antoine Winfield Jr. is progressing toward a return.
summary: Bowles opened with injury updates. An unnamed player did individual work and needs to do more Thursday. Jalen McMillan has no timetable, and Bowles said he hasn't been told anything. Antoine Winfield Jr. was in a full-contact jersey and is making good progress toward Sunday. Luke Goedeke did not practice, and Bowles said it looks slim for Sunday unless he does something Thursday and Friday. Baker Mayfield looked good in practice, and Bowles assumes he is better than last week, but he has been told nothing about how long the glove stays on. Bowles called running the ball the team's calling card, noted the lack of success at home, and called Bucky Irving the bell cow of late, with Gainwell also mentioned. He praised Ted Hurst's speed, confidence and routes, said the offense needs to get him the ball more, and credited Hurst and Chris Godwin Jr. for their blocking on a 11-pass day. On defense he credited practice emphasis and scheme understanding for the takeaways, said the pass rush is a work in progress, and acknowledged Kyle Pitts has hurt them. He also praised Drake London, Bijan Robinson, Michael Penix Jr. and Atlanta's rookie linebackers.

injuries.detail: Wore a regular full-contact jersey Wednesday; Bowles says he is making good progress toward Sunday.
Did not practice Wednesday; Bowles said his chances look slim if he does nothing Thursday and Friday.
No timetable; Bowles says he'll know when the medical staff tells him McMillan is ready and in uniform at practice.
Looked good in practice Wednesday, though he didn't throw much. Bowles assumes any issue from last week has improved. Wearing a glove, with no timetable given for how long.
Long-term knee injury with a minor setback. Bowles hopes he'll be ready in a couple of weeks.

signals.claim: Irving will remain the lead back and carry the main rushing load.
signals.note: Bowles called him the bell cow and said the team can ride him, a strong workload signal for fantasy.
signals.quote: he's been the bell cow for us the past couple of weeks

signals.claim: Hurst will be targeted more going forward.
signals.note: Bowles cited his improved speed and routes and said the offense needs to get him the ball more, which points to a growing role as the next receiver.
signals.quote: We just got to start getting them the ball a little bit more.

signals.note: Bowles praised his blocking in a low-volume passing game (11 attempts), so his production depends on how much the team passes.
signals.quote: I think him and Ted both did an outstanding job blocking and sustaining blocks.

signals.claim: Winfield is progressing toward playing Sunday.
signals.note: A full-contact jersey and good progress suggest he could return for IDP and DST managers.
signals.quote: He's making good progress for us.

signals.claim: Goedeke is unlikely to play Sunday unless he practices Thursday and Friday.
signals.note: A missing starting lineman could weaken the run game that Bowles called the team's calling card.
signals.quote: if he doesn't do anything tomorrow and Friday, it's going to look slim

signals.claim: Mayfield is healthier than last week.
signals.note: He looked fine in practice but has been wearing a glove and Bowles gave no timetable, so monitor his health.
signals.quote: he looked good in practice today, but not having to throw that much

signals.note: There is no timetable for a return, so he shouldn't be counted on soon.
signals.quote: I couldn't tell you. They hadn't told me anything.

topics.detail: Bowles called running the ball the team's calling card and said they play better when the run succeeds. They haven't had much success running or winning at home and need to turn that around.

Bowles credited practice emphasis and player buy-in for the takeaways, plus players better understanding the scheme and making plays within the calls. He singled out Tykee Smith and Jacob Parrish for aggressive plays.
The pass rush is a work in progress, improving week to week with players cleaning up for one another, but still needs some cleaning up.

Bowles called Kyle Pitts and Drake London superstars with no single priority, said Pitts has torched them recently, and described Bijan Robinson as dangerous in space. He praised Michael Penix Jr.'s arm, timing, mobility and ball security.

Bowles downplayed any edge from OC Zac Robinson's history with the Falcons, saying familiarity runs both ways with Jeff Ulbrich. He expects a cat-and-mouse game and says the Bucs need to change things up.
Bowles said he hasn't thought about the deadline and is focused on the next game, though he conceded the next two games could shape the team's approach.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Carnell Tate is sitting out Wednesday's practice with a shoulder issue, and Tyjae Spears and John Franklin-Myers are also not practicing for maintenance, so watch Thursday and Friday reports before the Bengals game.
summary: Saleh opened by saying three players were not practicing Wednesday. Carnell Tate has a shoulder issue, and John Franklin-Myers and Tyjae Spears are on maintenance days. The captions are muddled, so exactly who has the shoulder is somewhat unclear. He also said the punter, called Tommy, is still hurting from the game and the team signed Thomas Morstead to the practice squad as insurance. Most of the session was about Cincinnati, which he called the best team Tennessee will face all season, with Joe Burrow playing at an MVP level, Ja'Marr Chase as an elite weapon, and Tee Higgins as another top receiver. He described Sunday's defensive performance as an outlier ('laid an egg') that was about tackling and fatigue, not scheme. He defended the offense as reliable in the fourth quarter and praised Cam Ward's growth, citing good throws to Elic Ayomanor and Gunnar Helm. He said Tony Pollard and the offensive line have played well and that Tate is improving every week. Edge rushers Oluwafemi Oladejo and Keldric Faulk are not yet part of the pass-rush plan, though Saleh is bullish on both long term.

injuries.detail: Not practicing Wednesday with a shoulder issue. Saleh gave no game-status outlook, and the captions make the attribution slightly ambiguous.
Not practicing Wednesday, described as going through maintenance. No further detail was given.
Not practicing Wednesday, described as going through maintenance.
Still hurting from the game, with no timeline. The team signed a punter (Morstead) to the practice squad just in case, and Saleh said they would know more by the end of the week.

signals.claim: Tate will miss Wednesday's practice with a shoulder issue; his game availability is not yet determined.
signals.note: The WR1 rookie is a must-monitor on Thursday and Friday practice reports before the Bengals game.

signals.claim: Tate will keep improving and remain a central part of the passing offense.
signals.note: Saleh praised the rookie as a leading rookie receiver who bounces back after mistakes, which supports his usage if healthy.
signals.quote: He's been getting better every single week.

signals.claim: Spears is not practicing Wednesday while on a maintenance plan.
signals.note: A maintenance day is usually minor, but any limitation affects the backfield split with Pollard.

signals.claim: Ward is improving at holding the ball and taking hits to let routes develop.
signals.note: Saleh cited concrete progress in his decision-making, which supports Ward as a rising QB despite the record.
signals.quote: there's a lot of signs that he's been getting better

signals.claim: Pollard remains a productive lead back in the offense.
signals.note: Saleh singled him out for praise as the backfield situation is being watched with Spears limited.
signals.quote: I think Tony Pollard's been doing a hell of a job.

signals.claim: Ayomanor is a trusted target on key downs, including a fourth-and-eight conversion.
signals.note: Saleh highlighted multiple big throws to him as examples of Ward's growth.
signals.quote: still delivered a strike to Alec

signals.note: Saleh cited a Ward throw to Helm in the middle of the field as a good play, a small positive for his tight end role.
signals.quote: hits gunner in the middle of the field

signals.claim: Faulk is still developing as a pass rusher and needs to get stronger and more nuanced.
signals.note: This is IDP-relevant only: a long-term bet, not an immediate pass-rush boost.
signals.quote: He's going to be a hell of a football player.

signals.claim: Oladejo will not get a bigger pass-rush role soon, as others are ahead of him.
signals.note: IDP managers should not expect increased pass-rush snaps for now; he contributes mostly on special teams and against the run.
signals.quote: It's just not his turn yet.

topics.detail: Saleh called Burrow's play MVP-level, with quick decisions (about 2.4 seconds per dropback). He praised Chase's hands, route running and competitiveness, and said Higgins is also elite. He added that Cincinnati's run game, RPO system and high-low concepts make them the best team Tennessee will face all season.
Saleh blamed last week's poor showing on tackling and fatigue after a roughly 90-play game the week before, not on scheme. He called it an outlier and said he has full confidence in the defense.

He said the offense has repeatedly driven to tie or take the lead late in games and framed the team as close to winning, with the record not reflecting its progress. He added that it scored 24 points last week and must finish drives better in goal-to-go situations.
Saleh called trade talk part of the profession and said the team focuses on process and what it can control.
The team signed Thomas Morstead (whom Saleh knew from the Jets and 49ers) to the practice squad as insurance for the injured punter.
